proof_summary: Write the diagonal coefficient as \([x^M]F(x)^M\) and study the Frobenius quotient \(\Phi=F(x)^p/F(x^p)\); the divisor-sum identity controlling \(\sigma_2(ps)-\sigma_2(s)\) gives strong \(p\)-adic bounds on its logarithmic derivative. Expanding \(\Phi^M\) exponentially and combining factorial and coefficient valuation bounds proves divisibility by \(p^{2v_p(M)+2}\), which yields the claimed modulus on taking \(M=np^{k-1}\).
